title: Let a slow exchange rate end its pause, and only its own

blocks.text: The acquirer now offers cardholders the price in their card's currency. `QuoteRate`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/QuoteRate.java`, asks an exchange-rate service for a quote and pauses the transaction. The service has no timeout of its own, so the participant schedules one; without a rate, the purchase goes on and no conversion is offered. After `QuoteRate` the transaction pauses again while the card's issuer is asked.

Since the release, a few purchases a day are answered `91` (issuer unavailable) a few milliseconds after the issuer was asked. The issuer approves each of them shortly afterwards, so the cardholder is charged for a purchase the terminal reported as failed. Every one of them had a slow or failed quote.
Finish `Pending`, the nested class marked `TODO`: one `Pending` exists per transaction, and the quote, a failure and the timeout reach it on other threads, in any order. About ten lines in total.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with one session, with Q2 in the test's JVM. The exchange-rate service and the issuer answer when the tests say so, and the timeout is one second.

cases.says: a quote that arrives in time reaches the next participants with its rate
without a quote the participant's own timeout lets the purchase go on without a rate
a failed quote lets the purchase go on without a rate
a quote that arrives after the timeout must not resume the transaction again, or the issuer's pause ends before the issuer answers
a timeout that fires after a failure must not resume the transaction again: whether a rate arrived is not whether the pause already ended

origin.section: 15.6 A Paused Transaction Resumes Once, and an Extra `resume()` Is Kept for the Next Pause

concepts: A paused transaction must be resumed exactly once per pause; an extra resume() is kept and ends the next pause at once.
